source_quality.text_layer: partial; five empty or near-empty pages reconciled visually

task_reconstruction.summary: Task 1 asks for a material-adjustable forward model of wear after a stated use period.
Task 2 asks for traffic frequency, travel direction, and single-versus-parallel usage from observed depressions.
Task 3 asks for a practical field measurement set and acquisition method.
Task 4 asks whether inferred age, repairs, material, and daily crowd flow agree with external archaeological knowledge.

section_map.summary: Where Footsteps Collide compresses observable wear, spatial interaction, and historical inference into one concrete title.
The summary moves from archaeological need to scanning, three hybrid wear submodels, Bayesian inversion, numerical task results, repair layers, discrete events, and sensitivity.
The introduction first establishes why worn stairs carry historical information, then narrows the causes to material response, force dispersion, walking speed, traffic frequency, and habits.
The restatement decomposes the brief into wear simulation, usage inference, measurement design, and consistency checks against age, repairs, materials, and crowd flow.
The overview figure stages preparation, forward wear modeling, inverse estimation, advanced repair and daily-event extensions, sensitivity, and interpretation as an ordered pipeline.

Four assumptions pair each simplification with a justification, while Table 1 binds wear height, pressure, area, coefficients, traffic rate, mixture probability, footprint spacing, priors, and posteriors.
The data section converts a scanned point cloud into a registered tread grid and explains how acquisition geometry, reference planes, and measurement density support the wear surface.
Archard wear is transformed into a spatial probability wear equation, generalized to a two-dimensional tread, then supplied with bimodal, single-file, and side-by-side footprint densities.

A bounded logistic mixture links crowd intensity to single-versus-parallel walking, while front/rear foot partitions, Gaussian blur, random offsets, and explicit Euler updates distinguish ascent from descent.
Bayesian priors, data misfit, Laplacian smoothing, PSO initialization, local MCMC, and quantile intervals form an inverse workflow tested on noisy virtual observations.
A layered activation model represents renovation and re-exposure, after which a nonhomogeneous Poisson event model accumulates blurred and randomly shifted daily footprints.
Sensitivity discussion separates material coefficient effects from the context-dependent effect of the short-term side-by-side probability and flags time and arrival rate as influential.
The evaluation credits model integration and Bayesian uncertainty while limiting claims because of parameter burden, dependence on dense 3D data, and oversmoothing risk.
Eight references cover stair biomechanics, wear theory, finite elements, Bayesian analysis, image restoration, and particle swarm optimization.

contributions.summary: Derives a probabilistic wear rate from Archard's relation and assigns its spatial variation through foot-placement densities.
Links crowd intensity to a bounded single/parallel mixture through a stretched logistic curve.
Uses front/rear foot partitions to separate ascending and descending wear fields.
Combines PSO and local MCMC so a global search is followed by uncertainty quantification.
Represents renovation as layered wear with penetration and re-exposure.
Adds a one-day discrete-event model with time-varying Poisson arrivals and stochastic footprint placement.

dependency_graph.summary: 3D scan and registered tread coordinates supply the observed wear surface.
Archard wear plus traffic rate and foot-placement density supply the hybrid forward field.
Directional masks and traffic counts supply ascent/descent wear simulation.
Forward h_sim, observations, priors, and smoothness supply the posterior objective.
PSO supplies Theta star; local MCMC supplies posterior samples and intervals.
Layer state and renovation times govern activation; event arrivals and footprint maps govern one-day increments.

assumptions.summary: Treat walkers as normally weighted with evenly distributed pace and omit exceptional loads such as jumping.
Represent the unworn stair as an ideal horizontal plane and neglect local inclination introduced by the depression.
Assume pedestrians prefer the middle of the tread and use edge positions less frequently.
Treat microscopic sole slip during nominal rolling contact as an Archard-compatible sliding distance.
Treat environmental wear as a spatially uniform constant beta.
Use a symmetric Beta(4,4) body-center density for single-file traffic.
Represent ascent by front two-thirds foot contact and descent by rear two-thirds contact.
Use bounded priors and a local normal proposal around the PSO optimum.
Only the exposed layer accumulates wear until penetration or a new renovation layer changes activity.
Generate pedestrian events from a nonhomogeneous Poisson process.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Collect tread coordinates, height/depth relative to a reference plane, material information, and traffic context.
Use a 3D scanner to create a point cloud, register it, remove reference-plane height, and interpolate a regular grid.
Convert front/rear foot images to binary masks, blur them, resize them, and overlay randomly shifted copies.
Generate virtual observations on a grid with T*=257, kappa*=7.2e-5, segmented N_up/down, and Gaussian noise sigma=0.012.
Use 8000 sampled points, declared priors, lambda=5e3 smoothing, 40 PSO particles, 90 iterations, and 10000 MCMC steps with 2000 burn-in.
For daily simulation, specify lambda(t), binary footprints, blur width, random offsets/rotations, and per-event wear factor eta_e.

models.summary: Equation (1) preserves the Archard wear interface: Relate wear volume to load and sliding distance through a material coefficient.
Equation (2) preserves the height increment interface: Convert volume loss into local height loss per contact area.
Equation (3) preserves the traffic accumulation interface: Accumulate a single-step wear increment over arrivals in a time interval.
Equation (4) preserves the spatial allocation interface: Allocate total wear across the tread through a traffic-dependent density.
Equation (5) preserves the probabilistic wear equation interface: Define the one-dimensional probabilistic wear rate.
Equation (6) preserves the wear-source decomposition interface: Separate traffic wear from environmental wear.
Equation (7) preserves the improved PWE interface: Represent environmental wear as an additive constant in the lateral model.
Equation (8) preserves the two-dimensional IPWE interface: Generalize the wear state to a two-dimensional tread domain.
Equation (9) preserves the bimodal footprint density interface: Model left and right foot placements as two normal peaks.
Equation (10) preserves the BWPD wear update interface: Insert the bimodal footprint density into the wear equation.
Equation (11) preserves the Beta body-center density interface: Represent a center-preferring body location with a symmetric Beta density.
Equation (12) preserves the scaled Beta density interface: Map the unit-interval body-center density onto stair width.
Equation (13) preserves the marginal footprint density interface: Marginalize foot placement over uncertain body-center position.
Equation (14) preserves the side-by-side density interface: Superpose two body-centered footprint densities for parallel walkers.
Equation (15) preserves the traffic-dependent mixture interface: Mix parallel and single-file wear according to traffic intensity.
Equation (16) preserves the bounded logistic mixture interface: Keep parallel-use probability differentiable and bounded away from zero and one.
Equation (17) preserves the inverse objective preview interface: Preview a data, smoothness, and prior objective for inversion.
Equation (18) preserves the directional wear PDE interface: Separate ascent and descent through front/rear foot-contact maps.
Equation (19) preserves the explicit Euler update interface: Advance the directional wear field on a grid.
Equation (20) preserves the Laplacian regularization interface: Penalize sharp spatial oscillations in the simulated tread.
Equation (21) preserves the likelihood interface: Turn the energy into a likelihood kernel.
Equation (22) preserves the data-plus-smoothness energy interface: Combine Gaussian data misfit with the spatial penalty.
Equation (23) preserves the MAP objective interface: Express posterior optimization before local sampling.
Equation (24) preserves the layer wear state interface: Define the state tracked for each historical layer.
Equation (25) preserves the active-layer wear interface: Update a layer only while it is exposed.
Equation (26) preserves the active-layer time step interface: Advance the currently exposed layer in discrete time.
Equation (27) preserves the nonhomogeneous arrival rate interface: Represent baseline traffic plus daily arrival peaks.
Equation (28) preserves the Poisson event count interface: Sample the number of pedestrian events in each interval.
Equation (29) preserves the Gaussian footprint blur interface: Turn a binary sole mask into a smooth contact map.
Equation (30) preserves the random footprint placement interface: Translate and rotate a footprint for one event.
Equation (31) preserves the event wear contribution interface: Scale one event's contact map by its wear factor.
Equation (32) preserves the daily wear accumulation interface: Aggregate all pedestrian events into a one-day wear field.
The two-stage algorithm connects global heuristic search to posterior sampling, quantile intervals, and the parameter table.

verification.summary: Compare short-term large-use and long-term small-use wear fields under a fixed total visit amount.
Compare ascent and descent surfaces and report the relative location, area, and depth of indentation.
Recover known virtual parameters after adding Gaussian measurement noise.
Table 2 compares true values with posterior means, intervals, and relative errors.
Vary kappa and alpha_short and discuss the resulting wear curves.

results_trace.summary: Summary claims +/-5% ascent/descent differences, 30%-40% peak foot traffic, +/-5%-10% frequency uncertainty, +/-0.015 m depth error, and +/-10% material-wear uncertainty.
Ascending indentation is described as farther from the edge, wider, and shallower than descending indentation.
PSO reportedly converges around iterations 60-70 and takes about 25 minutes on an Intel i7.
Most virtual parameter errors are below 10%, while downstairs alpha_min has 16.7% relative error.
Most fitted surface residuals are claimed to be below 0.015 on the virtual observations.
Wear is reported as sensitive to kappa, total time T, and arrival rate N; alpha_short matters mainly in the short-term large-use regime.

writing_logic.summary: The summary uses need -> acquisition -> forward submodels -> inverse method -> task results -> advanced extensions -> sensitivity.
The introduction moves from archaeological value to physical causes, then enumerates decisions to recover from wear.
Each major assumption is paired with a justification before notation and data acquisition.
Forward-model prose repeatedly uses source law -> simplifying conditions -> transformed equation -> variable interpretation -> visual or downstream extension.
Inverse-model prose uses noisy observation -> prior and smoothing -> posterior -> PSO location -> MCMC uncertainty -> table.
Advanced-task prose moves from archaeological repair mechanism to layered update, then from daily arrivals to event-level footprint accumulation.
The paper closes with sensitivity, strengths, and weaknesses rather than overstating a general conclusion.

language_observations.summary: The summary assigns one method chain to each model before listing bounded task results.
On-one-hand/on-the-other-hand framing separates historical-use inference from structural and material inference.
Assumption/Justification pairs make the cost of each simplification visible.
In-the-context-of clauses adapt a general wear law to archaeological stairs before equations are transformed.
Where clauses immediately bind symbols to physical roles after each PDE-like relation.
If/then and meanwhile clauses define the desired limiting behavior before choosing the logistic form.
Algorithmic prose moves from masks to blur, scale, offsets, normalization, and output without hiding the state transition.
Step A/Step B labels make the global-to-local inversion handoff explicit.
Numbered application stages preserve the line from true values and noise to priors, computation, results, errors, and interpretation.
Conversely clauses distinguish parameter relevance between short and long usage regimes.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A visible chain from field measurement to multiple task outputs plausibly helps judges trace coverage, but it does not verify the claims.
A true-versus-posterior parameter table is a plausible clarity signal, although the self-generated observations limit validation strength.
Explicit strengths and weaknesses may improve credibility because the paper names data and smoothing limits.

weaknesses.summary: Equation (3) uses a sum indexed by dt even though N dt is already the event count; the discrete-to-continuous step is not derived rigorously.
Phi is printed as Phi(x;,N) in several places, leaving an empty argument and an unstable notation boundary.
Figure 4 retains the placeholder caption 'xxx', so its intended evidentiary role must be inferred from adjacent prose.
The model is repeatedly called a PDE while explicitly omitting diffusion and adjacent spatial coupling; it is a pointwise time update unless additional coupling is supplied.
Environmental wear is reduced to a constant beta without units, calibration data, or a check against weathering mechanisms.
The single-file body-center choice, Beta(4,4) assumption, and W-shaped depression description are not reconciled quantitatively.
Equation (17) previews a prior-augmented objective before the later likelihood and energy definitions, making the naming of E inconsistent across sections.
Algorithm 2 adds beta outside the Delta t multiplier even though Equation (19) multiplies the whole rate by Delta t.
Figure 12 retains the placeholder caption 'xxx' and the prose cites unresolved equation references '(??)'.
The heuristic step says it minimizes E(Theta), while the stated MAP objective is -ln p(Theta)+E(Theta); prior handling in PSO is therefore ambiguous.
The inversion uses observations generated by the same forward model, so parameter recovery is an internal synthetic test rather than external validation.
The reported posterior has one 10000-step Metropolis-Hastings run with no acceptance rate, multi-chain comparison, autocorrelation, or effective sample size.
Table 2 labels 90% intervals but reports posterior mean +/- interval without stating whether the value is a half-width or asymmetric quantile range.
Layer exposure and wear-through are described locally at (x,y), but the switching procedure also speaks of a single top layer; local versus global activation is not formalized.
The QR advertisement touches the right side of Equation (26), creating a mild source-overlay risk near its final terms and number.
The nonhomogeneous arrival peaks in Equation (27) have no fitted data, units, or identifiability discussion.
The event wear factor eta_e and footprint normalization are not calibrated to physical depth, so the one-day field has an unresolved scale.
Figure 14 and the prose do not provide a reproducible parameter grid or raw curves for all short-term and long-term sensitivity claims.
The claimed +/-5% to +/-10% task uncertainties in the summary are not consistently tied to Table 2's intervals or a common confidence definition.
No real staircase holdout, repair chronology, material assay, or raw scan is used to validate the integrated pipeline.

independent_extensions.summary: Validate the inversion on a real scanned staircase held out from calibration, with repeated scans and measurement error.
Formalize layer activation locally over (x,y), including partial penetration, removal, and dated repair records.
Estimate lambda(t), event wear factors, and footprint variability from counted traffic and controlled wear experiments.
Use multiple MCMC chains, posterior predictive checks, and model-discrepancy terms before reporting archaeological uncertainty.
Run a global sensitivity analysis over correlated material, traffic, time, smoothing, and mixture parameters.

candidate_rule_impacts.action: retain assumption-reason pairs, equation-interpretation clauses, matched regime contrasts, and bounded result handoffs

separate qualitative comparison, self-generated recovery, sensitivity, and external validation

unresolved_questions: What units and calibration make kappa, beta, and eta_e mutually consistent with measured wear depth?
What normalized density and event-count argument rigorously connects Equations (3)-(5)?
Why is the model called a PDE after diffusion and adjacent coupling are removed?
What field data identify the bounded logistic alpha(N) rather than merely motivating its shape?
Should beta in Algorithm 2 be multiplied by Delta t, as it is in Equation (19)?
How are the source placeholders for Figure 4, Figure 12, and unresolved equation references repaired?
Does PSO minimize E alone or the complete negative log posterior including -ln p(Theta)?
What acceptance rates, chain diagnostics, and posterior predictive checks support the reported intervals?
How are the summary's uncertainty percentages derived from Table 2 or another confidence definition?
How is local layer penetration reconciled with a single active top layer during renovation?
What observed daily counts calibrate lambda(t), its Gaussian peaks, and event wear factors?
Which raw curves and parameter grids reproduce Figure 14's sensitivity claims?
What independent staircase, repair history, or material assay validates the full inference pipeline?
